hypothesis_or_artifact: Section 14.3 / ADR-001. The power gate fired on raw excess-return dispersion against the dollar-volume-weighted universe, not on the residual dispersion of the registered Stage B inference (Carhart four-factor alpha), and the document says the latter 'will not [be] measure[d]' for a reason that does not hold on the store the power path actually reads.

claim_quote: the residual MDE would be lower than 49.35 by an amount this stage did not measure and will not measure, because measuring it after seeing BLOCKED is choosing a method by its answer.
evidence_summary: Supporting premise: 'The Stage A.1 number is measured against the universe benchmark rather than the Carhart residual, because a factor regression on uncentered data produces an intercept and the intercept is the alpha.' (DECISIONS.md:29-31). Carhart is not a method chosen after the answer; it is the registered inference: 'Carhart four-factor alpha on the resulting daily series, in Stage B.' (REGISTRATION.md:336-337); 'Stage B replaces this with the Carhart four-factor residual.' (REGISTRATION.md:353-354); primary contrast at :467-468. It was committed in 398755b at 2026-08-25T18:38:50-07:00, before the corpus (ccc9b13, 18:47:16) and before the power gate (cb17046, 19:11:45) -- git log, live repo, read-only. The stated obstacle does not apply to the store the power path reads: the dispersion store holds the series already centered on its own mean (src/insider/portfolio/returns.py:292-301; src/insider/power/dispersion.py:39-62, where CenteredSeries refuses an uncentered series). Regressing a centered series on centered factor returns without an intercept yields the same residuals as the intercept regression on raw data (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell); the residual standard deviation, which is the only dispersion the MDE consumes (src/insider/power/mde.py:50, :66), is therefore obtainable without ever producing the intercept, and the seal is not breached. The authors identify this as the one unmeasured conservatism that matters: 'The Section 14.3 conservatism is the only one large enough to matter. A Carhart regression would absorb the persistent size tilt between a mid-cap book and a mega-cap-weighted benchmark' (REGISTRATION.md:790-792). The benchmark is itself concentrated -- top-1 weight 7.02%, top-5 19.84% (reports/stage_a1/portfolio.json:25-26) -- so part of the measured 'tracking error' is the benchmark's own idiosyncratic variance, which a diversified market factor would not carry. Daily Fama-French three factors and the momentum factor are published free by the Kenneth R. French Data Library (no API, no fee); they are not an SEC source, so use would need a registered note against CLAUDE.md:61 ('SEC access only. Zero paid APIs.'), not a new budget.
recomputation: Beta-only adjustment from reported diagnostics (portfolio.json:20-22: sd_portfolio 0.014065, sd_benchmark 0.014575, corr 0.903981), n = 2,581 sessions. Excess sd = sqrt(sp^2 + sb^2 - 2*rho*sp*sb) = 62.95 bp, matching power.json:9. Residual sd after a single beta = sp*sqrt(1 - rho^2) = 60.14 bp. MDE_beta = 2 x 21 x 60.14 bp / sqrt(2,869.9) = 47.15 bp per month (N_eff held at power.json:8). So beta alone explains 8.7% of excess variance and leaves the verdict at BLOCKED. To reach DEGRADED the factor residual must be <= 51.02 bp daily (TE 8.10%), so size, value and momentum together would need to explain a further ~25.6 percentage points (34.3% cumulative) of excess-return variance. That is plausible for a mid-cap-tilted book against a mega-volume benchmark and is measured nowhere in the record. Scratch: recompute_mde.out.
would_resolve: Regress the centered primary series (and the centered equal-weighted series) on centered daily Carhart factors with no intercept; report residual SD, VIF at the registered lag 21, and the resulting MDE beside 49.35 and 34.29. This is a second-moment computation the existing guards permit. If the primary residual MDE lands at or below 40, the gate applied to the registered inference fires DEGRADED, not BLOCKED.
confidence_why: that the residual dispersion is computable without the first moment is certain; whether it crosses 40 is unknown, and the beta-only step does not.

hypothesis_or_artifact: The Section 0 power gate, primary series. evidence_summary: Same claim: 'The value-weighted book is concentrated by construction, and value-weighted was registered as primary before any number was visible.' (REGISTRATION.md:760-762). What was registered: 'Value-weighted primary.' (REGISTRATION.md:387), replicating Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski's value-weighted figure (REGISTRATION.md:49-50). What was run: 'value weighting is implemented as point-in-time median dollar volume from the formation window' (REGISTRATION.md:393-395; Section 14.2 at :566-576). Code: primary_weighting='value_weighted' (src/insider/config.py:136); weights are members.get(n, 0.0) (src/insider/portfolio/returns.py:102-103) where members_at returns median_dollar_volume (src/insider/market/store.py:100-108); no market-capitalization weight exists anywhere in the source. The authors stated the proxy's bias before measurement: 'It is more dispersed than market capitalization, so the book is slightly less concentrated and the tracking error slightly higher, which moves the minimum detectable effect toward BLOCKED rather than away from it.' (REGISTRATION.md:574-576); 'The substitution cannot flatter the design.' (DECISIONS.md:222). For a gate whose BLOCKED outcome is terminal -- 'Stage B is never written and the repo closes on the finding' (REGISTRATION.md:43) -- a substitution biased toward BLOCKED is the opposite of conservative with respect to the closure decision. The ex-ante direction sentence is internally contradictory, and the measurement resolved it against the 'slightly': 'more dispersed ... so the book is slightly less concentrated and the tracking error slightly higher' (REGISTRATION.md:574-575) -- a less concentrated book has lower, not higher, idiosyncratic tracking error. ADR-007 carries the same direction without the hedge: 'Dollar volume is more dispersed than market capitalization, so the book is less concentrated, tracking error is higher' (DECISIONS.md:219-221). Measured, n = 2,581 sessions: the 71.909-name book behaves like 29.73 effective names, top-1 weight 14.93%, top-5 33.79% (reports/stage_a1/portfolio.json:7, :23-24, :27; REGISTRATION.md:749, :752-754: 'Median dollar volume is heavily skewed, so weighting by it collapses a 72-name book into one that behaves like 30'). The route to the registered basis was named and not taken: dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 'was verified working' and was rejected because company_tickers.json 'lists only current registrants' (21 of 25 sampled issuers present) and shares are not split-adjusted (DECISIONS.md:204-212). A cheaper route exists inside data the corpus already holds: every Form 4 row carries ISSUERCIK and ISSUERTRADINGSYMBOL (src/insider/corpus/build.py:120, :123), giving a point-in-time symbol-to-CIK map from the filing stream with no survivorship; and the SEC's own DERA Financial Statement Data Sets (free, quarterly since 2009q1; sub.txt keyed by adsh and cik, num.txt carrying the EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding cover fact) supply shares outstanding by CIK without company_tickers.json. Both are SEC sources, inside the CLAUDE.md:61 boundary. Bracketing, n = 2,581 sessions on identical names: the most concentrated registered weighting gives MDE 49.3543 and the least concentrated gives 34.2897 (reports/stage_a1/power.json:12, :75); the BLOCKED bar of 40 lies between them. The registered primary weighting's MDE is unmeasured, and the closure attributes the failure to 'the registered primary' (REGISTRATION.md:837, :760-762, :860-863; DECISIONS.md:296-298) when the concentration is a property of the proxy that stood in for it.
recomputation: Inputs TE 9.9933% and MDE 49.3543 (power.json:10, :12); TE 6.8556% and MDE 34.2897 (power.json:73, :75); bar 40 (config.py:144). MDE scales linearly with TE at fixed N_eff (mde.py:50, :66), so the primary reaches DEGRADED at TE <= 8.10% (40/49.35 x 9.9933), a 19% reduction; the equal-weighted book sits at 6.86%. Implied per-name idiosyncratic volatility from TE x sqrt(effective names): 9.9933% x sqrt(29.73) = 54.5% for the proxy book and 6.8556% x sqrt(66.93) = 56.1% for the equal-weighted book, against the 30% planning figure at REGISTRATION.md:107-108. Whether a cap-weighted book lands below 8.10% TE is not determinable from the record; cap weights among the top 500 by dollar volume are also skewed. Scratch: recompute_mde.out.
would_resolve: Build the 126-session book with point-in-time market-capitalization weights via the free route above (Form-4-derived symbol<->CIK map plus DERA FSDS shares outstanding, restricting the cover fact to the quarter of the formation date to handle splits), run the existing power path on it, and report its MDE beside 49.35 and 34.29. claim_quote: On the identical names, the equal-weighted book holds **71.9 and behaves like 66.9**
evidence_summary: Same claim: 'Both books hold 71.9 names.' (REGISTRATION.md:863). 71.909 is the membership mean width before the ADR-009 drop (reports/stage_a1/portfolio.json:7, :91), computed by series.mean_width() at src/insider/portfolio/build.py:59. Its n is NOT 2,581: mean_width() averages over non-empty sessions only ('widths = [w for w in self.widths if w]', src/insider/portfolio/membership.py:46-54), and the reported coverage 0.995411 (portfolio.json:6; full precision 0.9954110898661568 at reports/stage_a1/corpus.json:173) pins that denominator at n = 2,603 non-empty sessions of the 2,615-session span. Effective names are computed on the priced book after the drop (src/insider/portfolio/returns.py:189-190, :195, :217), and the priced book averages 66.93 names (reports/stage_a1/power.json:16, :79, from widths.append(len(priced)) at returns.py:210), on n = 2,581 priced sessions (power.json:6, :69). For an equal-weighted book the inverse Herfindahl equals the name count, so 'behaves like 66.9' is simply the priced width, not a concentration statistic: the equal-weighted book is not behaving like fewer names than it holds, and almost all of the 71.9 -> 66.9 gap is the ADR-009 not-priced drop of 13,750 name-sessions (power.json:118 -- the block is keyed dropped_primary, but the two books hold identical names, so the counts coincide), with the small remainder belonging to the 22 sessions dropped as no_finite_member_return (power.json:117), which are exactly the 2,603 - 2,581 sessions separating the two denominators. For the primary, the like-for-like ratio is 29.73 of 66.93 = 44%, not 29.73 of 71.9 = 41%.
recomputation: book_effective_names 66.925223 (portfolio.json:111) versus book_width_mean 66.93 (power.json:79) -- equal to rounding, as an equal-weighted book requires; 29.731282 / 66.93 = 0.4442; 29.731282 / 71.909 = 0.4134.
